C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Handover
phases.goal: Short item leads end safely and a thin dispatcher keeps work moving without the sponsor.
phases.exit: H-01 to H-03 merged; one full bundle runs dispatcher → item lead → closing check → next lead with no sponsor action.

phases.name: Research
phases.goal: Questions that need reading, not writing, before they become items, a proposal, or a decline.
phases.exit: Every X row is done only when it becomes items, a numbered proposal, or a recorded decline with the reason -- never a report nobody acted on.

items.what: Before a lead stops it must prove four things: every sponsor message since it started has an ask row; every running agent is in the ledger with its worktree; the checkpoint matches the ledger; warmup --check reads ready. Exit 0 or a list of what is missing.

items.title: Background leads are visible and named apart from chat sessions
items.what: Every session the dispatcher starts in the background is started with `claude --bg --name <name>` so it shows by that name in `claude agents` and the desktop session list. Names follow a convention distinct from interactive chats: `bg · <project> · dispatcher` for the dispatcher and `bg · <project> · lead · P<nn> <item ids>` for an item lead (e.g. `bg · common-rules · lead · P26 C-03`). bin/handover --check and the tracker page list running background leads by name with their session id.
items.done: A background lead started by the dispatcher appears under its convention name in `claude agents --json`; a test pins the name format; the lead-prompt dispatcher form and H-03 proof run use it.
